plain_summary: Illustrative example only — replace every field. One sentence naming what the fix changes and why it closes the hole.
approach: Replace the string-concatenated BasicQuery with a parameterised Criteria query, adapting the catalog's CWE-943 canonical_approach to this repository's Spring Data MongoDB stack. Binding name/department as Criteria values (with Pattern.quote for the regex case) removes the caller's ability to inject query structure, closing the root cause rather than only the reported payload.

catalog_reference.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL/SQL Injection)

alternatives_considered: Blacklisting characters like { } $ ' in the input — rejected: the catalog's anti_patterns entry flags this as not closing the hole, since it addresses today's payload shape rather than the query-construction mechanism.
Adding request rate limiting only — rejected: mitigates abuse volume but leaves the injection itself exploitable at any rate.

affected_files.planned_change: Replace the StringBuilder-built BasicQuery with Criteria.where(...).is(...)/.regex(Pattern.quote(...)) chained conditions, keeping the same method signature and return type.

risk_notes: Pattern.quote() makes the search a literal substring match rather than a caller-supplied regex — confirm no legitimate caller relies on passing real regex syntax.
verification_plan: Replay the benign request from the issue (name=Ann) and confirm the same result set as before.
Replay the injection payload from the issue and confirm it no longer returns the full collection — it should return zero or an empty/literal match instead.
